text.en: A leech clings to a cow's leg in a pond and drinks blood without the animal even feeling the bite. Its body is built perfectly for this parasitic life.

The Indian cattle leech, Hirudinaria granulosa, is an annelid of class Hirudinea that lives in freshwater ponds, lakes and slow streams and feeds on the blood of fishes, frogs, cattle and humans.
Its body is soft, elongated and metamerically segmented into 33 segments and may reach 35 cm; the back is olive green and the belly orange.
It has an anterior sucker around the mouth (first five segments) and a posterior sucker formed by the last seven segments; the suckers help in attachment and locomotion.
The body is divided into six regions: cephalic 1-5, pre-clitellar 6-8, clitellar 9-11, middle 12-22, caudal 23-26 and the posterior sucker 27-33.
Digestion: three jaws with teeth make a Y-shaped wound, the pharynx sucks blood, the crop with 10 chambers stores it and digestion in the stomach is slow.
Saliva contains hirudin, which prevents blood clotting, and the leech also injects an anaesthetic so the bite is painless.
Respiration is through the moist skin by diffusion; circulation is by haemocoelic channels with four longitudinal channels and the fluid contains haemoglobin.
Excretion is by 17 pairs of nephridia and the nervous system is a nerve ring with a ventral nerve cord; the leech has five pairs of eyes.
Leech is hermaphrodite with 11 pairs of testes and a single pair of ovaries; fertilization is internal and a cocoon is formed around segments 9 to 11.
Parasitic adaptations include suckers, jaws, hirudin, a blood-storing crop and the absence of parapodia and setae.

problem.en: Why does a bleeding bite from a leech take longer to stop?

text.en: The salivary glands of the leech secrete hirudin.
So blood keeps flowing and the leech can feed continuously.

prompt.en: List four parasitic adaptations of the leech and the benefit of each.

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the leech has setae and parapodia (it does not)

points.en: Leech: phylum Annelida, 33 segments, two suckers, hermaphrodite.
Blood is stored in the crop; hirudin stops clotting.
Respiration through skin; excretion by 17 pairs of nephridia.
Clitellum on segments 9-11 forms the cocoon.
